title: Are one half, two fourths and four eighths the same length?
description: Three paper strips of the same length are folded into two, four and eight equal parts, and one half, two fourths and four eighths are shaded. The pieces are laid on one another to see where each shaded length ends, and Keeko doubts that two fourths is longer because its numbers are bigger.
teaching_notes: One idea: different fractions can name the same length of the same whole, and laying the pieces on each other shows it. Watch for students who think the fraction with bigger numbers is longer.

source: Three paper strips of the same length are folded: one into 2
video_script.why: The child sees on three strips of one length that one half, two fourths and four eighths reach the same place, and meets the name equivalent fractions.
video_script.substitution: none: the book's own three paper strips folded into two, four and eight equal parts
video_script.anchor: three paper strips of the same length, folded and shaded, as in the book
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says two fourths is longer because two and four are bigger numbers than one and two. Laying the fourth pieces on the half piece shows they fill it exactly, so the idea is broken.
video_script.payoff_line: One half, two fourths and four eighths are all the same length

final_answer.spoken: yes and yes, the three shaded lengths are equal

video_script.fraction_reading: one half, two fourths, four eighths, one fourth, one eighth
maths_rules: 3 strips of the same length; strip A folded into 2 equal parts, 1 shaded: 1/2
strip B folded into 4 equal parts, 2 shaded: 2/4
strip C folded into 8 equal parts, 4 shaded: 4/8
2 pieces of 1/4 fit exactly on 1 piece of 1/2, so 2/4 = 1/2
2 pieces of 1/8 fit exactly on 1 piece of 1/4, so 4 pieces of 1/8 cover the same length as 2 pieces of 1/4, so 4/8 = 2/4
1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8: the three shaded parts end at the same place, the middle of the strip
slip: Keeko thinks 2/4 is longer because 2 and 4 are bigger numbers than 1 and 2; the shaded lengths are equal
video_script.design: One idea: different fractions can name the same length of one whole. The three strips stay stacked with left ends lined up; the shaded parts end at one marker.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about three paper strips of the same length.
<bookmark mark='fold'/>One strip is folded into two equal parts, one into four, and one into eight.
<bookmark mark='shade'/>Then one half, two fourths and four eighths are shaded on the three strips.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Are the lengths one half and two fourths equal? Are two fourths and four eighths equal?

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

Each fold cuts a strip into equal parts.
<bookmark mark='ends'/>We look at where each shaded part ends, and not at the numbers.

<bookmark mark='same'/>They fit, so two fourths is the same length as one half.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: lay 2 pieces of 1/8 on each piece of 1/4; they fit, so 4 pieces of 1/8 cover the same length as 2 pieces of 1/4

<bookmark mark='fill'/>Each fourth is filled, so four eighths is the same length as two fourths.

beats.on_screen: Answer: a. Yes; b. Yes; so 1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8; the words equivalent fractions appear under the line

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>One half, two fourths and four eighths are all the same length.
The answer to both questions is yes.
<bookmark mark='name'/>Fractions that name the same length of the same whole are called equivalent fractions.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 2/4 is longer, because 2 and 4 are bigger numbers; the bubble is struck out as the 2 pieces of 1/4 lie exactly on the piece of 1/2

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble about bigger numbers appears
marks.fix: the two fourth pieces lie on the half piece and the bubble is struck out

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks two fourths is longer, because two and four are bigger numbers than one and two.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But bigger numbers only mean more parts, and each part is smaller.
The shaded lengths decide, and the pieces fit exactly.
